summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 165% to Rs 310.5 Cr, but gross margin fell to 21.6% from 44.4% and EBITDA margin to 8.3%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations for H1 FY27 was Rs 310.5 Cr, up 165% YoY and 24% over H2 FY26, with PAT of Rs 10.5 Cr (up 14%). Margins compressed as the mix shifted to lower-margin EPC and module sales, and the plant carried six months of fixed costs while manufacturing revenue reflected only about two to two-and-a-half months of output after ALMM-I enlistment in July 2026. Receivables rose to Rs 281.9 Cr from Rs 152 Cr in March, and borrowings reached Rs 189.1 Cr. Management reiterated H2 priorities of raising utilisation, recovering margins and cutting receivables, but declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave a PAT margin range of 5-6% for H2.

segments.name: Manufacturing (modules)
segments.commentary: Rs 113.4 Cr, 36.5% of revenue; 1.23 GW Miroli line commissioned March 2026, ALMM-I enlisted July 2026. Segment margin cited at 14-15%.

segments.name: C&I and Government (EPC)
segments.commentary: Rs 147.9 Cr, 47.6% of revenue; segment margin cited at about 25%. Two 50 MW AC contracts worth Rs 188.5 Cr and Rs 186.5 Cr won April 2026.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Rs 37.6 Cr, 12.1% of revenue; segment margin cited at 35-37% gross. Run rate about Rs 4-5 Cr a month excluding Kits.

segments.name: Solar Kits
segments.commentary: Launched during H1; about Rs 4.5-5 Cr revenue from mid-August to 30 September, reported within Residential. Management targets 15-18% gross and 10-12% EBITDA margin on Kits.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue guidance given; management said it was too early to guide.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at about 9-10%, with management saying H1 would have been about 9.5-10% without roughly Rs 4.5-5 Cr of idle-plant fixed costs.
H2 FY27 PAT margin expected to recover to about 5-6% as module sales return.
Finance cost expected to stay at current levels; no further material borrowing expected.
Large EPC contracts to be executed by end-March 2027; management expects 60-70% of the Rs 720.9 Cr order book to execute within FY27.
Plant utilisation was about 75-80% in September 2026 per management; captive consumption expected to rise to 50-70% over time.
capex_capacity: 1.23 GW automated module line at Miroli, Ahmedabad commissioned March 2026; produces TOPCon and PERC bifacial G12 modules up to 725 Wp.
ALMM-I enlistment in July 2026 allowed module supply to start; plant was largely idle before July.
Captive off-take of about 130 MW DC from the two 50 MW AC EPC contracts; about Rs 90 Cr of modules consumed captively in H1.
Domestic DCR cell supply tied up; management cited DCR cell capacity rising from 20 GW to 42 GW over six months.
Management said a fund raise is not currently planned, but may be considered for future growth.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 720.9 Cr: Rs 461.1 Cr EPC and Rs 259.8 Cr module supply. Module order book is for non-DCR (imported-cell) orders, which management says stay intact even if supply slips past the 31 December 2026 ALMM-II timeline.

Two 50 MW AC single-site ground-mount EPC contracts (Rs 188.5 Cr and Rs 186.5 Cr) reportedly subcontracted to two listed EPC companies at about Rs 165 Cr and Rs 175 Cr; management confirmed the subcontracting and said a margin of about Rs 35 Cr is secured.
Company has stopped bidding for distributed rooftop tenders and now bids for a small number of technically demanding site projects.

Residential run rate fell well below the previously guided Rs 10-12 Cr a month; management pivoted toward the Solar Kits distributor model and cited Gujarat state subsidy of about Rs 28,000 on top of central subsidy of Rs 65,000-70,000.
Management noted M10 modules (about 35% of ALMM-I listed capacity) are being phased out, which will reduce listed capacity; ALMM-I capacity was cited at about 217 GW nameplate.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the clients on the 50 MW EPC contracts, what are the payment terms, and what risks exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the clients are Maharashtra state-linked utility entities (named as Mahagenco). Payments are milestone-linked, with about 10-12 milestones and 15-30 days to collect after each.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing and finance cost rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most borrowing is already in place and finance cost should stay around recent levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables up to Rs 282 Cr when the prior call implied low working capital per project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most receivables are from the last couple of months of module supply after ALMM enlistment and that older AR has been largely recovered. It did not disclose the post-September collection amount and said it would share it separately.

qa_highlights.question: What was plant utilisation in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation was about 75-80% in September; the plant was largely idle for the first months until ALMM enlistment in July.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Solar Kits revenue, and where is it reported?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 4.5-5 Cr from mid-August to 30 September, reported within the Residential segment.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 9-9.5% EBITDA margin guidance from the last call still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was 8-8.5% due to under-utilisation (about Rs 4.5-5 Cr of idle cost) and that H2 should be about 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company plan an equity raise or main board migration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no equity raise is planned currently but it may raise funds for future growth if required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the residential run rate and why did it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was about Rs 4-5 Cr a month excluding Kits, or Rs 8-10 Cr with Kits in 1-2 months; the shift away from owned warehouses and fixed costs was cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the captive versus external split and the economics of the plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive consumption was small in H1 (about Rs 90 Cr of modules); management declined to share plant fixed-cost and break-even economics on the call, offering to respond separately.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kit distributor model and unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Kits bundle about 25 SKUs under the Solarium brand for installers; management targets 15-18% gross and 10-12% EBITDA margin, with inventory held until dispatch to installers.

qa_highlights.question: Will you guide FY27 revenue, and what PAT margin should be built for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance; for H2 it expects PAT margin to recover to about 5-6%.

risks_watch: Receivables of Rs 281.9 Cr against Rs 35.6 Cr cash, with milestone-linked EPC collections and no disclosed post-September collection figure.
Gross margin halved to 21.6% and EBITDA margin at 8.3%; H2 recovery to 9-10% depends on utilisation and absorbing fixed costs.
Subcontracting of the two 50 MW EPC contracts at a spread of about Rs 35 Cr: execution and delay risk is with subcontractors, and management said completion is targeted for end-March 2027.
Residential strategy pivot away from owned warehouses; run rate fell well short of the guided Rs 10-12 Cr a month, and the Kits model is at an early stage.
ALMM-II/DCR cell timeline (31 December 2026) and cell supply conditions; M10 product exclusion may cut listed capacity.
Management could not give plant break-even economics or the captive/external split on the call; these were deferred to separate responses.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic pivot and order book, but notably evasive on several specifics: it declined FY27 guidance, deferred break-even economics and post-September collections, and gave an inconsistent residential run rate. Management acknowledged the margin fall and the receivables build as priorities.

adds.what: 1.23 GW automated module line at Miroli, Ahmedabad (TOPCon and PERC bifacial G12 modules up to 725 Wp)

growth.why: No FY27 revenue guidance was given (withdrawn as too early); H2 FY27 EBITDA margin held at about 9-10% and PAT margin guided at 5-6%, backed by the 720.9 Cr order book (60-70% to execute in FY27) and the commissioned 1.23 GW Miroli line running at about 75-80% utilisation, but no explicit revenue growth figure.

oneOffs.what: Two 50 MW AC EPC contracts (Rs 188.5 Cr and Rs 186.5 Cr) won April 2026 and subcontracted at about Rs 165 Cr and Rs 175 Cr, with about Rs 35 Cr margin secured; these are non-repeating contract revenue
Plant largely idle until ALMM-I enlistment in July 2026, so year-ago manufacturing base is not comparable; H1 FY26 revenue of Rs 116.9 Cr is the base for +165% growth

quality.why: Revenue rose 165% to Rs 310.5 Cr, but growth is driven by a mix shift into lower-margin EPC and module sales from a near-idle plant base, plus large non-repeating 50 MW EPC contracts; gross profit grew only 29% and PAT only 14%, and receivables rose to Rs 281.9 Cr from Rs 152 Cr, so the headline growth is not recurring quality.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided H2 EBITDA margin to about 9-10% vs 8.3% in H1 and 7.5% in H2 FY26, as idle-plant fixed costs of Rs 4.5-5 Cr per half are absorbed at 75-80% utilisation; gross margin was 21.6% vs 44.4% a year ago, so the recovery depends on module mix returning.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 1.23 GW Miroli line was commissioned March 2026 and no further line was announced; management said a fund raise is not currently planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Plant utilisation was about 75-80% in September, the Rs 720.9 Cr order book has 60-70% to execute in FY27, and H1 revenue was Rs 310.5 Cr, up 24% over H2 FY26; no explicit volume number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation of 75-80% is near the 80% threshold, but the commissioned 1.23 GW line is recent, management said no fund raise is planned, and the plant economics were not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance and gave only H2 PAT margin of 5-6% and EBITDA margin of 9-10%, with receivables up to Rs 281.9 Cr and collections undisclosed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables of Rs 281.9 Cr vs Rs 35.6 Cr cash, residential run rate fell well below the guided Rs 10-12 Cr a month, and subcontracted EPC execution is delay-exposed with completion targeted for end-March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Solar Kits (about 25 SKUs) launched mid-August and generated about Rs 4.5-5 Cr by 30 September, with a target of 15-18% gross and 10-12% EBITDA margin on Kits.

rows.label: Rs 720.9 Cr order book executing in FY27
rows.why: Management expects 60-70% of the Rs 720.9 Cr order book (Rs 461.1 Cr EPC, Rs 259.8 Cr modules) to execute within FY27, with the two 50 MW EPC contracts targeted for end-March 2027.

rows.label: Receivables collection after Rs 281.9 Cr build
rows.why: Receivables rose from Rs 152 Cr to Rs 281.9 Cr, with milestone collections of 15-30 days after each of about 10-12 milestones, but the post-September collection figure was not disclosed.

rows.label: ALMM-II / DCR cell timeline 31 Dec 2026
rows.why: Module supply to DCR orders depends on DCR cell supply, with capacity cited as rising from 20 GW to 42 GW over six months; non-DCR order book of Rs 259.8 Cr is said to stay intact.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, the commissioned Miroli line and the H2 margin recovery to 9-10% EBITDA, but evasive on FY27 guidance, break-even economics, post-September collections and the residential run rate; analysts pressed on receivables and margins.
